purpose: Public, versioned medical knowledge metadata for local Clinical QC/Second-reader. Contains no patient data.
principles: Reference interval printed on the same laboratory report is the primary reference for HomeLAB QC when reliably extracted.
Abnormal, significant-risk and critical are different concepts; an out-of-range value is not automatically non-sendable.
Sensitive infectious results require a validated verification/notification pathway and must not be inferred from similarly named markers.
Clinical context can change interpretation; medication, fasting status, pregnancy, acute illness and prior trends should be requested when relevant.
The assistant is a second-reader for QC and does not independently diagnose, prescribe or change treatment.

glucose: When glucose and HbA1c appear discordant, verify timing, recent illness, therapy and factors that can affect HbA1c before drawing conclusions.
cardiovascular: Lipid results should be considered in overall cardiovascular-risk context; isolated lipid values do not establish cardiovascular disease.
kidney: Creatinine should be interpreted with eGFR, trend and clinical context when available; a single creatinine is not a complete kidney assessment.
liver: AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin are more useful as a pattern than as isolated values; medications and clinical context matter.
anemia: CBC indices and ferritin/iron studies should be interpreted together; serum iron alone is not sufficient to establish iron deficiency.
thyroid: Pregnancy, acute illness, thyroid medication and biotin supplementation can materially affect thyroid-test interpretation.
coagulation: PT/INR interpretation depends on anticoagulant use and therapeutic target; an elevated INR is not automatically a laboratory reporting error.
nutrition: Supplements, dose and timing can influence selected laboratory measurements; laboratory values alone do not prove dietary behavior or supplement use.
infection: Anti-HBs and HBsAg must remain semantically separate; reactive anti-HCV does not by itself establish current HCV infection.
